validated_results.title: Prediagnostic toenail selenium and risk of bladder cancer.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Prospective case-cohort study of prediagnostic toenail selenium and incident bladder cancer with an adjusted rate ratio reported.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest quintile of toenail selenium
extraction.population: men and women aged 55-69 years at baseline

sample_size.excerpt: The association between toenail selenium status and subsequent bladder cancer incidence was investigated in a prospective cohort study among 120,852 men and women aged 55-69 years at baseline (September 1986).

cases.excerpt: Follow-up for incident cancer was established by record linkage to cancer registries until December 1992. The multivariable case-cohort analysis was based on 431 bladder cancer cases and 2,459 subcohort members, for whom toenail selenium levels were available.

effect_size.excerpt: The age-, sex- and smoking-adjusted rate ratios (95% confidence intervals) for increasing quintiles of toenail selenium were 1.00 (reference), 1.09 (0.80-1.48), 0.55 (0.38-0.79), 0.63 (0.43-0.91), and 0.67 (0.46-0.97), respectively (P-trend < 0.01).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The age-, sex- and smoking-adjusted rate ratios (95% confidence intervals) for increasing quintiles of toenail selenium were 1.00 (reference), 1.09 (0.80-1.48), 0.55 (0.38-0.79), 0.63 (0.43-0.91), and 0.67 (0.46-0.97), respectively (P-trend < 0.01).

sample_size.excerpt: Over a median of 11 years, we followed 27 111 male smokers aged 50-69 years who were initially enrolled in the Alpha-Tocopherol Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study. During this period, 344 men developed bladder cancer.

cases.excerpt: During this period, 344 men developed bladder cancer.

timing.excerpt: All of these men had completed a 276-food item dietary questionnaire at baseline.
